references.text: The Lord says to Moses that he should not fear Og, king of Bashan, for the Lord has given him into their hand—the same promise and wording as in Deuteronomy 3:2
Describes Israel's victory over Sihon, the Amorite king who lived in Heshbon, which is referenced as an example in this verse
The Lord's promise to deliver Sihon and his land to Israel, and Israel's victory over him—the historical precedent mentioned in Deuteronomy 3:2
Moses reminds the people of the victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan—a reflection on this event
The Lord uses similar encouragement to Joshua: 'Do not be afraid'—the same type of divine assurance before battle
Rahab mentions how the Lord gave Israel victory over Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings—testimony to these victories
The psalm praises the Lord for striking down Sihon, the Amorite king—a praise for that victory mentioned as a precedent in Deuteronomy 3:2
Praises the Lord for the victories over Sihon, the Amorite king, and Og, king of Bashan—liturgical remembrance of these events
